as_told.title: Pentagon review of Vera Rubin Observatory imagery
as_told.place_text: Vera Rubin Observatory; secure facility in California

plain: The Vera Rubin Observatory, a large new telescope for surveying the sky, is said to be removing classified satellites and other objects from its data before anyone sees them. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel relays this second hand. She says the telescope "is going to remove a lot of classified satellites and other objects." Michels tells it in another episode, citing an article in The Atlantic. He says "all of Rubin's imagery has to be approved by the Pentagon," the US defense department, at a secure facility in California. Both raise it because it would mean that what scientists can see in the sky is filtered by the military.
